requirements.requirement: Run a long-running background worker as a managed systemd service named inventory-worker on node1
requirements.summary: cmd-6f7d3ffdfcea438e shows creation of /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service with an infinite-loop ExecStart, `systemctl enable --now` succeeding, and `systemctl status` showing active (running) with a main PID and a child sleep process. cmd-b1db18a9d1e54f01 confirms ticks continue to be appended to the log over time, and cmd-9f67670e535d43ac confirms the service survives a reboot as enabled+active with a fresh PID, demonstrating it is a persistent managed service rather than a one-off process.

requirements.requirement: Service is confined so it writes only inside /var/lib/inventory
requirements.summary: The unit uses ProtectSystem=strict with ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory (cmd-6f7d3ffdfcea438e, confirmed live via cmd-b1db18a9d1e54f01). The executor went beyond configuration inspection and ran a falsification test with an equivalent transient unit (cmd-637bbd1ed0804c62, cmd-4294c8338ac74f01): a write inside /var/lib/inventory succeeded while a write to /etc failed with 'Read-only file system', directly demonstrating the confinement is enforced, not merely declared.

NoNewPrivileges=yes is set in the unit and cmd-b1db18a9d1e54f01 shows /proc/<mainpid>/status reporting NoNewPrivs:1 on the live running process, directly confirming enforcement at runtime rather than just in the unit file.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1 (independent check): pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/data state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline (cmd-a40e2a69047f4ed9) captured boot_id 28ae5f98..., uptime, active service, and recent log ticks. Reboot was triggered via a backgrounded/disowned command that acknowledged immediately (cmd-9df66e4a255d4c47). Polling showed the old boot_id still present just after the trigger (cmd-fe3be637c0e54d34), then a connection timeout during the reboot window (cmd-58b1b1fcde59489e), then a new boot_id 2f82af98... with an advanced uptime start (cmd-9bf35f341ad44cc9). This is corroborated by the fixed lifecycle boot-identity observations, which independently show the same transition from 28ae5f98... to 2f82af98.... Post-restart, cmd-9f67670e535d43ac shows inventory-worker enabled+active with a new PID, a fresh log tick, and /var/lib/inventory ownership/permissions intact, completing the full before/disruption/after transition.

overall_summary: All three material task outcomes are satisfied with direct evidence: inventory-worker runs as a persistent, enabled systemd service; its sandbox (ProtectSystem=strict + ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory) was falsified live, proving writes outside the allowed path genuinely fail while writes inside succeed; and NoNewPrivs=1 was confirmed on the live process. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also fully and coherently demonstrated: healthy pre-restart baseline, an acknowledged reboot, a directly observed boot-identity change corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and full post-restart recovery of the service and data directory. Hygiene is good; the only blemish is a small unremoved test file left by a falsification probe inside the confined directory itself.
limitations: No evidence was captured showing removal of the transient falsification test's leftover file /var/lib/inventory/ok.txt.

The transient inventory-worker-writetest unit's cgroup/unit definition was not shown to be fully purged beyond systemd's --collect auto-cleanup, though this is expected default behavior and not independently verified.

operational_hygiene.summary: Nearly all executor commands were either directly required (user/dir creation, script and unit authoring, enable/start, reboot trigger) or read-only verification/polling. One minor unnecessary residue: the falsification test (cmd-637bbd1ed0804c62) wrote a throwaway file /var/lib/inventory/ok.txt that was never cleaned up afterward; this is low-risk (it sits inside the intended confined directory, is tiny, and doesn't weaken security or conflict with the service), but it is nonetheless leftover test residue from a diagnostic step rather than the task's own artifact. The transient systemd-run unit itself is self-collecting (--collect) and left no lingering unit. No failed services, no damaged package state, and no unsafe new exposure were introduced (listening-socket and package-health diffs between before-prepare and after-executor reflect only expected ephemeral ports/PIDs across the reboot).
